question: Thor v. City of Urbana (S.D. Ohio 3:26-cv-00196) — federal suit over the data-center zoning reversal is live
detail: Thor Equities and its four Urbana SPEs sued the City of Urbana, its City Council, and its Building & Zoning Appeals Board in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Ohio (Western Division) on 2026-06-19, docket 3:26-cv-00196-MJN-CHG. The complaint is ingested (data/documents/legal/thor-v-urbana/1.pdf) and read in data/extracted/urbana/litigation-thor-v-urbana.{yaml,md}. Eight counts: procedural + substantive due process (§1983), four declaratory-judgment counts invalidating the March-2026 emergency moratorium (Res. 2727-26) (Counts III–VI), the vested-rights count (VII), and the site-plan-denial count (VIII — the "incomplete" denial violated Zoning Ch. 1110). Thor claims a vested right to the data-center use that froze when it filed its 2026-02-13 site plan (Golf Vill. N. LLC v. City of Powell, 6th Cir.). Relief includes a Rule 65 injunction directing approval. This is the live legal spine of the Urbana story. OPEN — the outcome is pending; the nine complaint exhibits (the Apr-2025 ordinances, Res. 2727-26, Ord. 4635-26) and later docket entries are not yet in corpus.
